Class StagedContent

java.lang.Object
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.ihe.fhir.streaming.StagedContent
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, AutoCloseable
public final class StagedContent extends Object implements Closeable
Document content that has been extracted from a FHIR request body while that body was still being read from the wire. So, neither the base64 text nor the decoded byte array is ever materialized on the heap by the FHIR parser.

Content up to memoryThresholdBytes is kept in memory, anything beyond that is spilled into a temporary file. Either way the content is handed over to the XDS side as a DataHandler that e.g. CXF can stream into an MTOM attachment. Large documents never require a contiguous heap allocation.

An instance may own a temporary file and must therefore be closed. The owning StagedContentRegistry does that at the end of the request.

  • Method Details

    • sink

      public OutputStream sink()
      Returns the sink to decode the base64 content into. Closing the returned stream does not release the staged content, it only signals that no further content will be written.
      Returns:
      output stream accepting the decoded document content

    • isSpilled

      public boolean isSpilled()
      Returns:
      true if the content was large enough to be spilled into a temporary file

    • dataSource

      public jakarta.activation.DataSource dataSource(String contentType)
      Exposes this content as a DataSource for the XDS request. The content type is not known at staging time (in FHIR JSON, contentType may appear after data) and is therefore supplied by the caller.
      Parameters:
      contentType - MIME type of the document
      Returns:
      data source streaming this content

    • getSha1Hex

      public String getSha1Hex()
      The lower-case hex encoded SHA-1 of the decoded content, computed while it was streamed past. Available once the sink has been closed. This is the digest XDS expects in, so it can be used to verify a client-supplied without a second pass over the content.
